title: Schedule Impact Days Allowed Against the Guarantee on a Retrofit Project
content:
# Schedule Impact Days Allowed Against the Guarantee

Change orders on a project under Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects state the calendar days they add to the work, and which of those days extend the guaranteed period depends on why the change arose.

## Rule

Where the issued change orders state schedule impact on a change the owner asked for or on a schedule acceleration, the guaranteed period is extended by every impact day stated on the issued change orders, the owner having asked for the work that moved the date.

Where the issued change orders state schedule impact on a concealed condition or a code requirement and none on a change the owner asked for or a schedule acceleration, the guaranteed period is extended by the impact days stated on the concealed conditions and the code requirements alone, a supplier's days not being the owner's to have.

In every other case the guaranteed period is extended by half of the impact days stated on supplier substitutions, that is by 50 per cent of them, rounded down to a whole day, the delay of a substitute the owner accepted being shared between the two.

## Reading the change order reasons

The impact days are read from the schedule impact stated on each issued change order of the project, grouped by the reason the change arose: owner requested and schedule acceleration on one side, concealed condition and code requirement on the second, supplier substitution on the third.

| Impact days stated on owner-requested or acceleration changes | Impact days on concealed condition or code requirement changes | Impact days on supplier substitutions | The guaranteed period is extended by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | 4 | 3 | 13 days, every impact day stated |
| 0 | 4 | 3 | 4 days, the concealed condition and code requirement days alone |
| 0 | 0 | 7 | 3 days, half of 7 rounded down |
| 0 | 0 | 0 | nothing |

## Worked case (hypothetical)

A project carries three issued change orders: one for a concealed condition stating 5 impact days, one for a supplier substitution stating 9, and one for a change the owner asked for stating 2. Because an owner-requested change states impact, every impact day counts and the guaranteed period is extended by 16 days. Had the owner-requested change stated none, the extension would be the 5 concealed condition days alone.
